clue.text: He's to accept rise as arranged, but she's 20 dn

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the letters of He's open up to hold the rest

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: arranged here means put in a new order, so the letters of rise are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A man is to take on an uprising, but a woman is named in a will.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to 20 down, LEGATEE, someone left a bequest; a woman due to inherit is one. The 'He's' at the start is wordplay, not the man of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who inherits is named in a will to receive property, which is what a legatee is.

clue.text: Erica's man, heart-broken

parts.note: he is the pronoun standing for a man

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so the pooled letters are reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: Erica's boyfriend is left heartbroken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erica' reads as a woman's name, but it is the botanical genus of heath plants. 'broken' scrambles HE plus HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the Latin genus name for heaths, the low moorland shrubs with bell flowers.

clue.text: The language one used over cold beast in charge

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another comes before it

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: Someone describes the tongue they once spoke over a cold creature that was in command.
explanation.definitionFit: Icelandic is the Norse tongue spoken in Iceland.

clue.text: Speak well of previously regressive group

parts.note: ex- means former, from before

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the word for group is read the other way

parts.note: a lot is a group or set of things, as at auction

explanation.surface: Someone praises a set of people who were formerly backward-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone highly is the meaning of the formal verb extol.

clue.text: Assistant blundering into people practising black magic

indicators.note: blundering means stumbling about clumsily, so the letters of Assistant are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A clumsy helper stumbles into a coven of devil-worshippers.
explanation.definitionFit: Devil-worshippers who hold black masses are followers of Satan.

clue.text: Hibernating insects -'about a thousand altogether

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the two insects stand around the thousand

parts.note: a dor is a dung beetle, an old crossword insect
an ant is an insect
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Sleeping insects, roughly a thousand of them in all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insects' supplies two insects, DOR (a beetle) and ANT, and 'about' has them surround M.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal hibernating is inactive through the winter, asleep and inert.

clue.text: There are many about on a ship's deck

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
re means about or concerning
SS stands for steamship, a prefix on ships' names

explanation.surface: A count of passengers milling about on a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like part of a ship, but it is the verb: to dress a ship is to deck her out with flags.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to adorn or decorate, as in decking the halls.

clue.text: An old clerk's office

parts.note: clerk is the old sense, a clerk in holy orders, a clergyman, and his office is his parish post

explanation.surface: It sounds like the workplace of an elderly office clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: A clerk in holy orders is an old term for a clergyman, and a rector is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The post or term of a parish priest of the Church of England, a rector, is so called.

clue.text: On the other hand it could make a profit

parts.note: a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Alternatively, it might turn a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Again can mean besides or moreover, introducing a contrasting point, like conversely.

clue.text: Staggering like the salvage collectors?

explanation.surface: Someone is unsteady, like the rag-and-bone men collecting scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: Totters are British rag-and-bone men who collect and sell scrap; the second reading treats the answer as an adjective meaning like them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tottery means unsteady on one's feet, and whimsically it is what a scrap dealer's trade is like.

clue.text: Experienced at keeping key record

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so the word at holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: D is a musical key
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone is practised in holding on to an important document.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is skilled or proficient through practice.

clue.text: Keen to get rent changed, give voice

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters of rent are put in another order

parts.note: to chant is to give voice in song

explanation.surface: Tenants protest loudly to get the rent altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen in the sense of sharp or incisive, as of wit or criticism.

clue.text: Banners perhaps causing a wrinkling of the brow

definitions.text: Banners perhaps causing a wrinkling of the brow

parts.words: Banners perhaps causing a wrinkling of the brow
parts.note: banners are the big front-page titles of a newspaper, and they may be worrying, while lines on the head are wrinkles on the forehead

explanation.surface: Alarming newspaper banners make readers frown.
explanation.definitionFit: Banner titles in a paper are large-print captions, and split in two the word also means lines across the forehead.

clue.text: Wildcat strike in no uncertain fashion!

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Workers walk out unofficially, and make no bones about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a 'wildcat strike', an unofficial walkout; 'strike in no uncertain fashion' just colours the scene, with the cat sitting inside nO UNCErtain.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard, a big wild cat of Central Asia, is also called by this name.

clue.text: Equestrian appendage

explanation.surface: A horse lover and an added extra.
explanation.definitionFit: An equestrian is a horseman; an appendage to a document, such as an added clause, is also so called.

clue.text: Really friendless, calling for indulgence

indicators.note: friendless means with the friend taken away, so a word for friend is removed from Really

parts.note: a mission is a calling or vocation

explanation.surface: Someone truly alone longs to be pampered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friendless' removes ALLY (a friend) from REALLY, leaving RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Indulgence in the church sense is the pardon of sins, and remission is forgiveness of them.

clue.text: An old sailor, a right-minded man, dancing

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor
a Tory is a British Conservative, someone on the political right

explanation.surface: A veteran seaman and a conservative fellow are dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' looks like a verb on the men, but it defines the adjective; saltatory comes from Latin saltare, to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltatory describes leaping or dancing, from the Latin word for jump.

clue.text: Cuts one in fifty classes

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the one goes within fifty plus classes

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
rates are classes or grades, as in first-rate
an ace is a one in cards or dice

explanation.surface: One in fifty school classes is cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerates means tears or gashes the skin.

clue.text: Firm beat — is not fluctuating

indicators.note: fluctuating means shifting about, so the letters of beat is not are mixed up

explanation.surface: A steady rhythm that does not waver.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm in the sense of stubborn, unyielding in one's view.

clue.text: Cradle-song?

parts.note: a cradle song is a lullaby, but cradling a baby means swaying it to and fro, so the song is one for swaying to

explanation.surface: A lullaby.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocking a cradle gives a punning name for the loud popular genre with guitars.

clue.text: Broadcast ensuring servicemen will join unit in time

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of British servicemen

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the unit goes within the time

parts.note: a date is a time
I is the Roman one, a unit

explanation.surface: Troops join a unit just in time to go on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to send out in all directions, as a broadcast spreads.

clue.text: Quiet sovereign offering support to an artist

parts.note: ease is quiet, rest and calm
a sovereign is a pound coin, abbreviated L for libra

explanation.surface: A peaceful monarch helps out a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign was a British gold pound coin, and L is the pound sign's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the stand that holds a painter's canvas.

clue.text: A barrier, in general, to a beneficiary

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the barrier goes within the general

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
a gate is a barrier

explanation.surface: An army commander stands as an obstacle to an heir.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is someone left a legacy in a will.

clue.text: The people giving Danish leader, partial backing

indicators.note: the leader of the word Danish is its first letter
backing means going backwards, so the word for partial is reversed

parts.note: some means partial, a part of

explanation.surface: Citizens give a Danish politician partial support.
explanation.definitionFit: Demos is the Greek word for the common people, the populace.

clue.text: He laid down the law in the doctors' quarters

parts.note: MOs are medical officers, army doctors
e is a stand-in for the, as in Ye Olde
E and S are compass quarters; here S is one quarter

explanation.surface: Someone imposed rules in the medics' living area.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical prophet received the Ten Commandments and gave Israel its law.

clue.text: "Crossing the _____ Thames at Bab-Lock-hithe" (Arnold)

parts.note: the printed quotation has a gap before Thames: the missing word from Matthew Arnold's poem The Scholar-Gipsy fills it

explanation.surface: A line of Victorian verse about a ferry on the upper river.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a blank before 'Thames'; the line in Arnold's The Scholar-Gipsy calls the young upper river a youthful one, so the answer is the missing adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A young lad is the usual sense; Arnold uses it of the narrow, young upper river.

clue.text: Several notes needed to get a bit of fish!

explanation.surface: Playing music to earn a piece of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A run of notes up or down is a musical scale; a fish's skin is covered with small plates of the same name.

clue.text: Punctilious page or groom

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper and punctilious

explanation.surface: A fussy pageboy or bridegroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' looks like a noun beside 'page', but it is the verb, to tidy oneself up.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom oneself is to preen or titivate one's appearance.

clue.text: Alsatians worried the attacker

indicators.note: worried, like a dog with a bone, means shaken about, so the letters of Alsatians are jumbled

explanation.surface: German shepherd dogs savaged the intruder.
explanation.definitionFit: An attacker is one who assails, an assaulter.

clue.text: Pile into it, though it's far from suitable

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the pile is put within it

parts.note: nap is the raised pile on cloth such as velvet

explanation.surface: Someone throws a heap into a pile though it does not fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate.

clue.text: Intrinsic feature of a European city church

parts.note: Essen is a city in western Germany
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A characteristic part of a church in a Continental city.
explanation.definitionFit: The inherent nature or core quality of something.

clue.text: A body of soldiers after drink first and foremost

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the soldiers follow the drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A troop of soldiers go for a drink first of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest or paramount, ahead of all others.
